subject: Acme: Post-call recap & request for procurement/SLA/discount exceptions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Acme: Post-call recap & exception request

Quick recap from this morning's discovery with Acme (Jenna Park, Tom Reynolds) — note the ask below that will need internal sign-off.

What they told us:
- Economic buyer: Jenna Park (VP Product) — cares most about reliability and predictable pricing.
- Procurement lead: Tom Reynolds (procurement@acme.com) — tight timeline, wants legal + procurement review in ~2 weeks.
- Requirements: 99.9% uptime SLA, data residency in us-east, and standard SOC2 evidence.
- Decision criteria: latency under 200ms P50 for a 1k token call, predictable per-token unit economics, and contractual SLA credits.

Their ask:
- Formal 99.9% SLA with credit schedule (they may push for termination on repeated breaches).
- 20% discount off list if they sign a 12-month commitment today (they said finance can move fast if terms are acceptable).
- A procurement exception to our standard 30-day net payment / PO process (they prefer 60 days).

Attachments: redwood_procurement_exception_form.pdf (application/pdf)

What I need from you:
1) Can we consider a one-time procurement/payment terms exception to 60 days for this account?
2) Is legal comfortable with a 99.9% SLA + limited credit schedule (I can propose caps)?
3) Do we have appetite to offer up to 20% off for a 12-month committed ARR of ~ $360k/year?

I recommend we aim for: 20% discount conditioned on annual commit, SLA 99.9% with credits capped at 10% of annual invoice, and no termination right for SLA credits unless repeated breaches across three months.

I'll need explicit approvals by EOD Friday to keep their procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0172
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call recap & exception request

Thanks for the clear summary, Marissa. A few quick questions before I sign off: 

- Confirmed ARR / expected yearly spend if they sign 12 months? You flagged ~$360k — is that net of discounts?
- If we offer 20% do we have precedent for that at this deal size (I think we have some comps at 15% for first-year commits).
- Payment terms: 60 days is a commercial ask — finance (Vivek) please confirm if we can allow that as a one-off and whether we need additional credit checks or PO language.

On SLA: 99.9% is fine if credits are capped and breach definitions are tight. Suggest we draft an SLA that:
- Uses rolling 30-day windows for availability computations;
- Caps credits at 10% of monthly invoice;
- Allows remediation windows before any termination rights.

If Finance and Legal are comfortable, I can approve the commercial exception (discount + payment terms) contingent on legal sign-off of the SLA language.

-Aditya
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call recap & exception request

Thanks, Marissa. I reviewed the high-level asks. A few legal/security items we need clarified before I can sign off on an SLA exception:

1) Exact SLA language requested by Acme (they mentioned termination for repeated breaches). We should avoid termination rights tied solely to availability unless it's a material breach.
2) Do they require 24/7 SRE escalation or a named POC? If so, that increases operational cost.
3) Data residency: can we guarantee us-east residency for this tenant in our Hosted offering, or do they require Dedicated / Private?
4) Please attach SOC 2 Type II report and our data processing addendum; procurement will ask for these.

I've prepared a draft SLA clause that caps credits at 10% of monthly fees and removes termination rights for availability alone; attaching draft for review.

Attachments: SLA-exception-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

If Marissa can confirm the procurement contact and deadline, I will review and give conditional approval pending Finance's confirmation on credit/payment terms.

-Lauren
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Acme: procurement details + requested approvals (answers inside)

Looping back with answers from Acme and our proposed final approvable terms.

Acme confirmations:
- Procurement contact: procurement@acme.com (Tom Reynolds)
- Timeline: procurement review next week; they can sign the order by 2026-07-28 if terms are agreed this week.
- Committed ARR if we take 20% off and 12-month term: ~ $360,000 annual (net of discount).
- Data residency: they said Hosted in us-east is acceptable as long as we confirm data does not leave region and we provide SOC2 report.

Proposed internal approvals requested:
1) Commercial: 20% first-year discount conditioned on a 12-month minimum commit (Aditya approval requested).
2) Finance: allow one-time payment terms exception to Net 60 for this customer, contingent on PO and standard credit checks (Vivek approval requested).
3) Legal: approve SLA language per attached draft (no termination for availability alone, credits capped at 10% monthly, remediation windows) and confirm we can provide SOC2 documentation (Lauren approval requested).

Attachments: redwood_procurement_exception_form.pdf, SLA-exception-draft.docx
Related links: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-137

If we get explicit approvals from Aditya, Vivek, and Lauren by EOD Friday I will send the revised proposal and SLA to Acme and ask them to route to procurement.

Thanks — Marissa
